en: The *Ratnavarṣa-dhāraṇī-sūtra* Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Great Wisdom under Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the kingdom of Kauśāmbī at Kuntaka.
Ānanda was there together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus,
as well as with a great multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, in the kingdom of Kauśāmbī, there was an elder named Candraprabha (Moonlight),
whose sense faculties were tranquil and whose mind was serene.
There were many men and women, as well as numerous male and female servants,
who, having achieved pure faith,
went to where the Buddha was and prostrated themselves at his feet.
Having circumambulated [the Buddha] a hundred thousand times, he withdrew to stand to one side.
With palms joined in reverence, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I wish to question the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"I have a few matters of doubt;
I only pray that the Great Compassionate One will look upon me with pity and grant me permission.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the elder, saying:
"Ask whatever you wish;
I shall explain it for you so that your heart may find joy."
At that time, having heard these words, the elder was filled with joy and leaped for gladness, saying:
"World-Honored One, how may sons and daughters of good family who are currently impoverished become wealthy and abundant?"
"May all those who have illnesses be freed from illness.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the householder Candracchattra, saying:
"For what reason do you ask such a question?"
Then that householder addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"World-Honored One, we who live as householders have many dependents, yet our wealth and resources are meager;
it is difficult for us to provide for them."
Furthermore, there are many illnesses.
We pray that the World-Honored One will reveal the essential points of the Dharma,
so that the poor may forever be freed from poverty.
The storehouses and treasures were all completely filled.
He provided for his wife, children, and kinsmen within the household; whenever anyone came to seek anything, he would surely give with joy, acting as a great donor.

May all their granaries, treasuries, and storehouses be abundant with gold, silver, precious gems, wish-fulfilling *maṇi* jewels, *vajra* stones, and various rarities such as conch shells, *śilā*, red pearls, agates, and other kinds of golden treasures, never to be exhausted.
He provided for his relatives and extensively practiced giving to benefit sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the elder Candracchattra, saying:
"Son of good family, in the past, incalculable eons ago, I encountered a Buddha, a World-Honored One."
He is named Tathāgata Vajradharasāgaraghoṣa, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
From that Tathāgata, he received this Ratnavarṣa Dhāraṇī;
having received it, he upheld, recited, contemplated, reflected upon, rejoiced in it, and extensively explained and disseminated it for others.
By the power and majesty of this dhāraṇī,
if any son of good family— or any non-human being, yakṣa, rākṣasa, bhūta, piśāca, kumbhāṇḍa, uṣadāraka, pūtana, kaṭapūtana, or the like— should give rise to an evil mind, [they shall be subdued].
They shall be unable to cause harm.
Furthermore, if there are various ghosts who wish to come and harass them by devouring their fat, marrow, pus, blood, mucus, saliva, or excrement and urine,
they shall be unable to create obstacles.
The Buddha told Candracchattra:
"If there are sons of good family who, with a devout mind, keep it in their thoughts,
hold it in their hands, write it down, merely hear its name, uphold it, rejoice in it, or extensively expound it for others..."
Those sons and daughters of good family shall enjoy peace and security and receive all manner of happiness for a long night,
because they possess the abundant and secure provisions for yoga.
If there be anyone who wishes to uphold this Vajra-ratna-varṣaṇī Dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain these benefits].
One should make offerings to all Tathāgatas and,
with single-minded devotion, recite and maintain [the mantra] for one night, two nights, or three nights.
The devas who revere and have pure faith in the Triple Gem will all rejoice;
they will immediately rain down wealth, treasures, grain,
and wheat for the sake of that Dharma-preacher who recites and chants.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying: *Namo bhagavate vajradhara-sagaravegajaye tathāgatāya*.
Tadyathā oṃ sruve vadaravati dṛgācaḍre acapatre udgatani udbhinani svāhavati dhanyava.

60. *Āvartaya sarvasattvavijayamanusmara svāhā.* 61. The Buddha addressed the elder Candracchattra:
This is called the Jewel-Rain Dhāraṇī.
By the power of this dhāraṇī, illnesses,
famines, epidemics, and karmic obstructions are all completely extinguished.
If a son or daughter of good family first makes offerings to all the Tathāgatas,
they should then recite and maintain this dhāraṇī continuously for one day and one night without interruption.
In that household, there shall rain down treasures the size of a large man,
and all calamities and misfortunes will be completely extinguished.
Therefore, son of good family, you should receive, uphold, and recite this Ratnavarṣa Dhāraṇī.
He extensively analyzed and expounded it for others.
"Excellent, World-Honored One!
the householder Sunetra said, and hearing what the Buddha had spoken, he rejoiced with leaping joy.
"I have now received from the Buddha this Jewel-Rain Dhāraṇī;
I shall receive, uphold, read, and recite it, and extensively explain and analyze it for others.
At that time, the elder Candracchattra, having received the Buddha's instruction, [acted accordingly].
Having circumambulated the World-Honored One one hundred thousand times,
they joined their palms in reverence, prostrated with their heads at his feet, and departed with joy.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda.
"Go to the house of the elder Sucandra and observe that all his various storehouses— filled with diverse wealth, grain, precious gems, and all manner of requisites— are now completely full."
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, having received the Buddha’s instruction,
went to the great city of Kauśāmbī and approached the house of the elder Candra.
Having entered, he saw that all the storehouses were completely filled with wealth and treasures.
Having seen this, his heart was filled with great joy and he returned with leaping exultation.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, marvelling at such an unprecedented occurrence and feeling exceedingly joyful, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, by what causes and conditions is the storehouse of the householder Sunetra so full?
The Buddha said,
“Good son, the householder Sunetra possesses pure faith in me.”
Uphold this Ratnavarṣa Dhāraṇī and proclaim it for the sake of all sentient beings. Therefore,
Ānanda, you must uphold this dhāraṇī and teach it extensively to others.
With my Buddha-eye, I observe all the worlds— including devas, humans, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas—
and none among them can create obstacles for one who upholds this Vajra-ratna-varṣaṇī dhāraṇī.
Why is this? Because the Tathāgata does not speak otherwise,
and these mantra-syllables are indestructible.
Sentient beings who lack roots of goodness will not even hear the name of this dhāraṇī,
let alone write it down, receive and uphold it, or read and recite it. Why is this?
This is proclaimed as the true word of all Tathāgatas;
it is rejoiced in by all Tathāgatas;
it is praised by all Tathāgatas.
It is proclaimed by all Tathāgatas;
it is planted by all Tathāgatas.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Excellent, World-Honored One!
He then spoke in verse with these sublime gāthās:
"The Buddhas are inconceivable, And the Buddha-dharma is likewise so."
Pure faith is inconceivable, and its karmic fruition is likewise so;
O Jñānavatī, you who possess all-knowledge! O Dharma King, neither born nor extinguished, you have already reached the supreme further shore; I bow my head to the Buddha, the Valiant One.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda,
having heard the Buddha speak this *Ratnavarṣa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
leaped for joy and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Blessed One, what should this essential teaching be named?
How should we, now, uphold this sutra?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
This sutra is titled "The Questions of the Householder Candra.
You should receive and uphold it;
it is also titled "The Attainment of All Treasures and Hidden Stores."
It is also called the *Dhāraṇī Teaching on the Rain of Jewels Praised by All Tathāgatas*.
You should receive and uphold it.
When the Bhagavān had finished speaking this sutra, [the assembly rejoiced].

The immeasurable bhikṣus, as well as the bodhisattvas, gods, humans, asuras, and the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The heart mantra is: Oṃ vasudhare svāhā. The heart-of-the-heart mantra is:
Oṃ śrīvasu svāhā. The small heart mantra is: [Oṃ vasu svāhā].
